events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: A Hero Marches

options.text: Encourage the city's praise of the hero.
He is a soldier first and foremost.

events.text: [character] marches at dawn, his forces completely wiping out the enemy. Already known as a hero, further legends start to spread in [city] of his abilities. Will you encourage or restrain this idol worship?

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Champions of the Storm

options.text: Very good!
Have these champions teach what they’ve learned to our other forces.
Arrange to have their commander join the court.

events.text: Trees bend low and break against the [event] winds. Some are lifted up out of the earth, roots and all, while others splinter and snap mid-trunk. Fierce as it is, the storm cannot break your soldiers, who fight with fury and without relent, destroying all in their path. Long before the winds subside and calm returns to the sea and to the battlefield, the legend of the [unit] spreads across [rival].

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Defending [rival]

options.text: If the tide turns against us, we will be ready.
We cannot afford to be distracted by a few raiders.

events.text: With fighting inside [rival] borders, [character] urges a concerted effort to rally forces and maintain defenses on all fronts. Of course, to properly organize such efforts would take time, and not be without cost.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Eye of the Storm

options.text: We will agree to this truce.
You are there to fight.

events.text: The night before battle, [character] meets with the opposing general. A swift-riding messenger lets you know that he has managed to secure terms for a truce, if you are willing to accept. Will you agree to your diplomat general’s idea?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Feigned Retreat

tip: As general: Can Rout (attack again) after defeating a Unit in Combat

requirements.label: Uncouth / Impulsive
tip: The leader must have one of: Uncouth; Impulsive

options.text: Restraint be damned! Tactics are simple. You just keep attacking until they are dead.
[character] is right. Knowing when and where to strike is half the battle.

tip: As leader: +10% Unit Trait Modifier / Mounted
As general: +25% Unit Trait Modifier / Mounted

options.text: We don't need to fight like them; we just need to defeat them.

events.text: Your Generals describe the [tribe] as a force of nature on the battlefield: A swell of horses and men crashing across the earth, launching forth rolling waves of arrows and splitting the air with thunderous cries. Just as it seems like the two forces might meet, the Huns pull back like the tide, drawing the enemy to chase in their confusion. Few survive a second wave. After his success, [character] believes he can use the [tribe] tactics to lead your forces to greater triumphs. The other generals dismiss him, saying there is nothing to learn from such barbarians.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Flanking Maneuver

options.text: Take them by surprise!
We can’t risk it.

events.text: Your general and pathfinder, [character], has discovered a hidden route through the local lands that could allow your forces to surprise the enemy with a flanking maneuver to trap and completely rout them. However, the path is treacherous and it would take some time to move all of your warriors. Will you order your troops to march this route?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Greedy Conduct

options.text: "Perhaps you have a point... " Sigh deeply. "Send the bodies as a - what do people call it? - ah, yes, a goodwill gesture."
Nothing comes free, and it is time [rival] and the rest of the world learned that.

events.text: [character] looks distraught. "Surely we can't ask [rival] to pay for the return of their dead? Not only would we further antagonize [character], but I fear for the reputation we would gain among gods and men."

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Ignoble

options.text: Make it known [character] acts with my personal blessing. Make it pointedly known to those who might think of causing trouble.
I shudder to think what such a man would do with even greater power.

events.text: That is the only name you are given. [character]. He has risen to lead an entire mercenary [unit] unit, yet no one knows anything of him beyond the sort of far-fetched tales told to frighten children. Such a man, such a reputation, could be useful. Or an unmitigated catastrophe.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Infamous General

options.text: Troubling...

events.text: The villainous ways of [character] are becoming known far and wide as tales of the misdeeds of his [rival] warriors and their willingness to inflict any cruelty spread across the world.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Inspired Troops

options.text: “Hold formation and never surrender!”
“Fight with everything you have!”
“Protect your comrades!”

events.text: [character]’s inspiring words have roused your armies to go above and beyond. Before battle, he prepares to speak to the troops. “Every day we rise and fight to keep [rival] safe. Once more we are needed and once more we will heed the call. Stand with me my friends, and whatever happens…”

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Legend of the Sword

options.text: Encourage the legend of the sword.
The strength comes from [character].

events.text: [character] led his forces to a glorious victory, completely routing the [rival] forces. Tales quickly spread about his mysterious blade, saying that it seemed to move as if guided by the divine. [character] has done well, but is the strength from the sword or the wielder?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Put to the Sword

options.text: [rival] needs men like [character].
Enough. There must always be boundaries.

events.text: [character] has proved himself even more capable than you hoped in putting down the [family] rebels. Skirmishes turn to slaughters as the rebels are lured into ambush after ambush, and eliminated to a man. The merciless campaign, and the collateral damage, have a price, however. [city] grows ever more unhappy under the thumb of [character] enforcement.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Cost of Cowardice

options.text: [character] is an enemy of the state.
Hunt him down.

events.text: As the battle begins, [character] is nowhere to be seen. Leaderless and in disarray, the [rival] forces are quickly routed and left to be picked off. This cowardice is nothing short of treason. What will you decree?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Cost of Pride

options.text: Learn from this, [character].
The problem was your men, we will find you new troops.

events.text: The battle is vicious and bloody. Even once victory is assured, [character] keeps pressing forwards, attacking time and time again. On the fourth charge, a surprise flanking move by the few remaining enemy forces breaks his troops. The few survivors retreat back. [character] has routed the enemy, but was the cost worth it?

events.author: Benjamin Gautron
events.name: The Greatest Chariot Battle of All Times

options.text: I found the mass of chariots in whose midst I was, scattering them before my horses!

events.text: Today was a glorious day for [rival]! Near [city] the vile [rival] and their numberless cavalry ambushed the royal column and tried to take by treachery what they couldn't obtain through valor. They routed our warriors and isolated our [title], who was deserted and surrounded by enemies. The greedy [rival] thought they had won and were plundering our camp. They thought they were celebrating victory! But, at the darkest hour, Amun master of victory came to our [title]. [character] was before them like Set in his moment! The army rallied around him and charged again! The [title] chased the [rival] from our camp and slaughtered a great many of them. They scattered before us, abandoning their chariots to flee across rivers, dispersing as fast as swimming crocodiles! In spite of the [rival]'s treachery, today we won the largest chariot battle the world has ever seen!

events.author: Benjamin Gautron
events.name: The Greatest Chariot Battle of All Times

options.text: I found the mass of chariots in whose midst I was, scattering them before my horses!

events.text: Today was a glorious day for the [rival]! The accursed [rival] were marching their innumerable cavalry hosts to threaten our land and our people. We misled them, lured them close to [city], where the [title] had mustered our glorious chariotry. Only too late did they realize their mistake! We struck like thunder and terror filled their hearts. [character] was like Tarhun before them! We scattered their warriors like chaff in the wind, routed their vaunted army and plundered their camp. Their [title] barely escaped with his life! Their numberless horde was defeated and they had to retreat. [city] is safe and we won the largest chariot battle the world has ever seen!

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: To the Front

options.text: I can't fault [character] dedication and bravery.
This kind of chaos is unacceptable. If there is a way to force [character] early retirement, I will find it.

events.text: [character] has taken to the role of General with great zeal... and to the concept of chain of command with notably less. Reports of his movements and engagements - bolstering the line wherever fighting is fiercest - continue to bring as many surprises as those of the enemy.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Unleashed

options.text: Let loose.
Retain composure.

events.text: As the battle rages, an urge strikes you. To lose all restraint, fight from the front and let your enemies feel the hammer of your blows.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Unyielding General

options.text: [character]'s tenacity is an inspiration.

events.text: No matter how many times they are attacked, [character]’s troops refuse to give ground. His rallying cries mean that the troops keep fighting well beyond what would normally be possible.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Word from [city]

options.text: Support [character] proposals.

events.text: Word reaches you in the field that, as you manage affairs on the front, a capable man by the name of [character] has taken a directing role back at the royal court. [character] advocates for honing the capabilities of existing [rival] forces while directing resources to the [rival] heartlands.
